components.finding: BPI (every nontrivial set-sized Boolean algebra has a prime ideal), Boolean ideal and filter extension and the set Ultrafilter Lemma are defined at def:p01-bpi-principles on top of written definitions of Boolean algebra, filter, ideal, prime ideal and ultrafilter; arbitrary-set-variable propositional compactness (any set V, finite formulas over p_v with bottom, top, not, and, or; total valuations V->2; finitely satisfiable => satisfiable) is defined at def:p01-bpi-propositional-compactness. Part 2 adds the set-indexed language Form(P) and the same scheme.

Both directions are written over ZF with no choice principle beyond the one stated: (a) set Ultrafilter Lemma => compactness (annex 293-322: truth sets in 2^V, recursion identities, proper generated filter, one ultrafilter extension, characteristic homomorphism, valuation by Replacement, induction on formulas); BPI => compactness via the written ZF equivalence (annex 198-289). (b) compactness => Boolean ideal extension (annex 324-350: one variable per algebra element, operation and ideal formulas, finite satisfiability from the written finite local lemma, kernel of the resulting homomorphism is a prime ideal), then the written four-way equivalence gives BPI and the Ultrafilter Lemma. Every lemma used (duality, quotient, finite local evaluations, four-way equivalence) has its proof written in the annex.

The theorem itself states that both directions hold for arbitrary variable and formula sets and that the fixed enumerable-alphabet statement has a separate choice-free proof that must not be used as the arbitrary-set principle (body 185-188); the remark and annex explain the different domains and the enumeration/binary-tree route (body 191-203, annex 352-356). The countable route itself is on the route: the enumerated Lindenbaum proof of thm:prop-compactness (inherited-02545-02664 72-96, inherited-02665-02809 44-66) and the ZF binary-tree method def:p06-countable-compactness-route with Konig's lemma; Part 2 (supplement 37-42, 70-72) and the Part 6 dependency table (330-335) repeat the separation.

All three listed subcomponents are supplied at their standing: definitions as hbdefinition entries, the equivalence as a proved theorem (status proved=annex:p01-bpi-propositional-compactness with written proofs), and the distinction inside the theorem statement and its remark. The ZF base and arbitrary-set hypotheses are kept. The original note (Ultrafilter Lemma present but never linked to compactness) is answered: the Ultrafilter Lemma definition now points to its statused theorem whose part 3 gives the compactness equivalence, the Part 1 section opens from def:ultrafilter-lemma to the compactness bridge, and the Part 2 compactness theorem names def:ultrafilter-lemma and points to the Part 1 proofs.
